entry.title: Width and Depth Limits Commute During Training in Linear Residual Networks
entry.summary: Recent work established that the infinite-width and infinite-depth limits of residual networks commute at initialization when residual branches are scaled by $1/\sqrt{depth}$. In particular, the network output converges to the same limit whether width and depth tend to infinity sequentially or jointly. We extend this commutativity result to training in linear residual networks. Under the same $1/\sqrt{depth}$ residual-branch scaling (Depth-$μ$P) and the $μ$P width parameterization, we prove that, for any fixed number of gradient-descent steps with gradient clipping, the network output converges in $L^2$ along every joint width--depth growth path as both width and depth tend to infinity. Consequently, the infinite-width and infinite-depth limits commute throughout any finite training horizon. Without gradient clipping, the corresponding $L^2$ convergence does not hold in general, but we establish the weaker convergence in probability.

entry.title: Illumination-Aware Active Perception for Spacecraft Inspection
entry.summary: Harsh and rapidly varying orbital illumination introduces failure modes during spacecraft inspection. Existing planners rely on line-of-sight inspection metrics which perform occlusion checks against a known target and conflate geometric visibility with task-relevant information. These metrics overlook illumination effects including eclipse, self-shadowing, and specular reflection from spacecraft materials and tend to declare components as inspected despite the corresponding images lacking sufficient information. We propose an inspection-planning framework that replaces geometric visibility with a learned measure of camera information derived from a classifier variational autoencoder (VAE) that operates directly on the captured image. The encoder model is trained to classify spacecraft surface components from rendered patches, and its total latent variance is used to learn the varying illumination of said components, replacing binary visibility checks with a continuous, image-grounded quantity. We evaluate the approach by implementing a Guidance, Navigation, and Control architecture in a photorealistic physics simulator, and vary lighting and viewing geometries with multiple orbits. We show that, although all approaches successfully maximize their own objective, our approach results in better illumination: a mean brightness of $0.57$, with $81.6\%$ of observations above $0.25$, compared with $0.02$ ($3.0\%$) for geometric planning with an illumination band and $0.04$ ($6.0\%$) for purely geometric planning.

entry.title: The algebraic theory of non-archimedean intertwining periods
entry.summary: We develop an algebraic theory of local intertwining periods for symmetric pairs $(G,H,θ)$ over non-archimedean local fields $F$ of characteristic different from $2$, and finite-length representations of Levi subgroups of $G$ with coefficients in an algebraically closed field $R$ of characteristic different from the residual characteristic of $F$. For open orbits this algebraic version is essentially contained in the work of Blanc and Delorme. The theory relies on a crucial new uniqueness result, extending a result of Blanc and Delorme for open periods, which asserts that an admissible intertwining period is the only $H$-equivariant linear form extending the corresponding integral on the space of well-supported sections. In the group case it recovers at once the results of Dat on algebraic intertwining operators. Our algebraic construction does not require the unimodularity hypothesis imposed in the work of Matringe--Offen--Yang. When $R=\mathbb{C}$, we also remove this assumption in the classical non-archimedean analytic setting, and prove convergence of intertwining periods for all symmetric spaces. At the same time we extend the context of the whole theory in the following manner: we allow $F$ to be of positive odd characteristic, we allow twisting characters in the periods, and we allow $H$ to lie between $(\mathbb{G}^θ)^\circ(F)$ and $G^θ$. Finally, in the algebraic setting, we obtain explicit polynomial bounds for the singularities of intertwining periods, and compute them in a concrete case.

entry.title: Test-Time Prompt-Agnostic Decomposition
entry.summary: Test-Time Prompt Tuning (TPT) adapts large pretrained models to unseen target distribution shifts by updating only lightweight prompt tokens. Existing TPT methods are effective, but they mainly optimize each prompt update locally. Across test-time steps, prompts updated at the current step are reused for the corresponding predictions and updates, so noisy or biased unlabeled objectives can accumulate and destabilize the prompt-update trajectory. We identify two failure modes: magnitude expansion, where updates move the prompt too far, and directional drift, where consecutive updates point in inconsistent directions. To analyze and control these failures, we propose Test-Time Prompt-Agnostic Decomposition ($\mathtt{TPD}$), which characterizes observed prompt-update trajectories from a dynamical-systems view and decomposes base prompt updates into magnitude and direction. $\mathtt{TPD}$ computes a spectral radius to measure update expansion and decomposes update directions into persistent, oscillatory, and residual components. Building on this decomposition, Adaptive Koopman Control ($\mathtt{AKC}$) regulates update magnitude by shrinking updates under expansive recent dynamics, while Hankel Update Router ($\mathtt{HUR}$) refines update direction by preserving persistent components and suppressing oscillatory and residual components. Together, $\mathtt{AKC}$ and $\mathtt{HUR}$ produce a stabilized prompt update. As a prompt-agnostic framework, $\mathtt{TPD}$ can be plugged into visual and text TPT methods without modifying the backbone, prompt architecture, or adaptation loss. Experiments on 15 datasets show that $\mathtt{TPD}$ consistently improves 10 baselines, with accuracy gains of $3$--$8\%$ for visual prompts and over $2\%$ for text prompts.

entry.title: Beyond feature attribution: Recovering latent interaction structures in machine learning models via localized CBFI
entry.summary: Background: Understanding individual predictions in complex tabular models remains challenging, as existing additive frameworks like SHAP and LIME often obscure structural logic by absorbing nonlinear interactions into individual feature scores. Exposing these latent interaction structures is essential for automated auditing in high-stakes environments where understanding the logic of model behavior is as essential as predictive accuracy. Methods: To address this limitation, we introduce the localized case-based feature importance (CBFI) framework. Unlike traditional numerical attribution, our method decomposes instance-specific predictions into structurally distinct components, effectively separating independent main effects (G1) from pure interactions (G4) to capture explicit feature synergies and provide a principled approach for diagnosing feature combinations. Results: Comprehensive experiments on wine quality classification and medical insurance regression demonstrate that localized CBFI successfully disentangles complex interactions hidden by additive models. Furthermore, fidelity tests and synthetic ground-truth benchmarks confirm that the identified interactions correspond precisely to the nonlinear structural dependency patterns embedded in complex architectures, including gradient boosting and deep neural networks, thereby successfully shifting the explainable AI paradigm from simple numerical attribution to the recovery of interaction-driven contributions.

entry.title: A Hierarchical Method for Environmental Sounds Recognition in Complex Acoustic Scenes
entry.summary: Environmental noise identification is essential for noise control, yet conventional single-stage classifiers suffer from class confusion under imbalanced multiclass conditions. This paper proposes a lightweight hierarchical model integrating a Frequency-Time Adaptive Network (FTANet) with a two-stage classification mechanism. FTANet employs parallel asymmetric one-dimensional convolutions to capture temporal dynamics and frequency-band distributions, while adaptive fusion attention (AFA) enhances discriminative acoustic features. In the first stage, FTANet classifies sounds into five coarse-grained categories covering 25 fine-grained classes. In the second stage, samples are routed to the corresponding category-specific classifiers for fine-grained recognition. On a self-constructed dataset, FTANet achieves 95.45% coarse-grained accuracy with only 0.2004M parameters. On UrbanSound8K, it achieves 79.24% mean accuracy and 80.37% mean F1-score in ten-fold evaluation, outperforming compared convolutional models. Field tests on the Tianjin Online Acoustic Environment Monitoring Platform yield 87.94% coarse-grained accuracy and 97.21% conditional fine-grained accuracy for natural sounds correctly routed to C2. The complete hierarchical model achieves 87.18% overall accuracy and 87.40% weighted-average F1-score, demonstrating its feasibility for urban environmental noise monitoring.

entry.title: Embedded minimal surfaces with three ends associated with the Hoffman-Osserman catenoids
entry.summary: For every positive integer $g$ and every Hoffman-Osserman catenoid in $\mathbb{R}^5$, we construct a complete embedded minimal surface of genus $g$ that is not contained in any proper affine subspace of $\mathbb{R}^5$. These surfaces can be viewed as higher-codimensional analogues of the Costa-Hoffman-Meeks surfaces, associated with the union of the corresponding Hoffman-Osserman catenoid and the plane containing its waist circle. We provide explicit Weierstrass data for these surfaces. Our construction can also be interpreted as restoring conformality to a deformed Costa-Hoffman-Meeks immersion by introducing two additional harmonic coordinate functions.

entry.title: A General Framework for Leggett--Garg Violation in Neutrino Oscillations and Matter Effects
entry.summary: The Leggett--Garg inequality (LGI) constrains temporal correlations under the assumptions of macrorealism and noninvasive measurability. We study the four-time quantity \(K_4\) for two-flavor neutrino oscillations using a pseudo-density matrix (PDM) under static conditions, instead of non-invasive measurement. With this approach, it becomes possible to examine a Horodecki-type criterion for the temporal Pauli-correlation tensor. The Horodecki criterion had been proven for CHSH inequality (R. Horodecki et al. Phys. Lett. \textbf{A200}, 340), For any unitary qubit evolution, the corresponding scalar is \(M_R=2\). Although, this result characterizes the correlation tensor and the optimized temporal construction, it does not imply that a fixed flavor observable violates the LGI at every neutrino energy or baseline. We therefore evaluate \(K_4\) explicitly for flavor measurements in matter of constant density. The numerical examples illustrate how matter effects modify the temporal correlations, with a pronounced matter--vacuum separation near the MSW resonance for the chosen parameters and generally smaller differences in the selected off-resonance cases. This finding motivates further investigation of matter-induced temporal correlations in atmospheric neutrinos and their potential relevance to future studies with long-baseline and atmospheric-neutrino experiments, including DUNE and Hyper-Kamiokande.

entry.title: Transporting Quantiles to Codebook: Scalable Vector Quantization without Codebook Collapse
entry.summary: Effective discrete representation learning with VQ-VAE serves as a fundamental component of modern autoregressive generative models. However, it is widely known to suffer from codebook collapse and inefficient code utilization. To address this issue, we propose FlowVQ, a simple yet effective alternative to standard vector quantization by formulating neural quantization as a joint modeling and clustering process. Specifically, we learn the latent space using a lightweight flow matching model alongside training, corresponding to a probability flow ODE that transports an often fixed well-behaved source distribution while preserving probability mass. Based on this, we define the codebook C_1 by transporting even-quantile partitioned prior codes C_0 from the source space through the learned flow, and obtaining the Voronoi centroids under the induced distribution, leading to a structured discretization. We evaluated on image tokenization and generation, as well as on two tasks requiring high-precision tokenization, demonstrating scalability and improved expressivity of the codebook with full utilization.

entry.title: A proof of P != NP (New symmetric encryption algorithm against any linear attacks and differential attacks)
entry.summary: P vs NP problem is the most important unresolved problem in the field of computational complexity. Its impact has penetrated into all aspects of algorithm design, especially in the field of cryptography. The security of cryptographic algorithms based on short keys depends on whether P is equal to NP. In fact, the security requirements for cryptographic keys are much stricter than those for P$\neq$NP, the security of the key must ensure not only a sufficiently high computational complexity to crack it, but also consider the security of each bit of the key, while fully avoiding the effectiveness of various attack methods. In this paper, we innovatively propose a new encoding mechanism and develop a novel block symmetric encryption algorithm, which be named Eagle, whose encryption and decryption can be completed in linear time. The key consists of 10 variables, for the attacker, in the case when only the plaintext-ciphertext correspondence is known, the problem of cracking the key is equivalent to solving a system of equations about ten unknown variables together with some implicit variables which are generated by the encryption process. In this paper, we will prove that there is no universal algorithm without brute-force searching at least one variable during the process of verifying four of the ten variables whose computational complexity is not greater than solving the ten variables. After performing elimination the implicit variables, the problem of verifying the four variables will be equivalently transformed into a series of general quintic equations about one variable with coefficient given by other four variables, according to the conclusion that ``there is no algebraic solution to quintic equations", we can't establish a system of algebraic equations only containing the other four variables......

entry.title: Explore More, Validate Less: Efficient Reflective Prompt Optimization
entry.summary: Reflective prompt optimization improves instructions using task feedback, but coupling candidate generation with full-validation-based selection can make search costly and sequential. We propose a two-stage framework that decouples reflective candidate-pool construction from validation allocation. During construction, sampled parents first answer training questions, and groups of their saved responses guide parallel reflection and revision. Each child is screened on its group's questions against the corresponding parent scores. Improving, nonduplicate prompts enter the pool and can become parents without full validation. After construction, an exploration policy selects candidates from the frozen pool under a fixed full-validation budget, and the prompt with the highest measured validation score is returned. This separation allows candidate-pool size and validation budget to be set independently. We evaluate random selection and a multilayer perceptron with similarity-based exploration (MLP + similarity) on five benchmarks using Qwen3.5-9B and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. With 100 retained candidates and 20 full validations, our framework improves over the initial solver by up to 11.22 percentage points. MLP + similarity improves over the initial solver in all ten comparisons, although neither selection policy consistently outperforms the other. These results support separating reflective search from budgeted validation while leaving room for stronger candidate-selection policies.

entry.title: Implications of exclusive photon leptoproduction measurements for the proton charge-radius puzzle
entry.summary: In the present study, we extend our previous analysis of the proton electromagnetic form factors (FFs) extracted from exclusive photon leptoproduction (EP) measurements in kinematic regions where the Bethe--Heitler (BH) process dominates the cross section by including all currently available high-precision EP data from CLAS and Hall~A Collaborations. Using the same phenomenological framework, we investigate the consistency among the different datasets, determine the proton electromagnetic FFs within several fitting scenarios, and extract the corresponding charge and magnetic radii. A significant tension is found between the CLAS 2018 measurements and the remaining EP data, with the low-$|t|$ region playing a dominant role in this tension. We systematically investigate this behavior through $|t|$-cut scans and assess its impact on the extracted FFs and radii. For all analyses, the extracted proton charge radius is smaller than the Particle Data Group average and most determinations based on elastic electron--proton scattering. However, the results are consistent, within uncertainties, with the PRad measurement and muonic hydrogen spectroscopy. In contrast, the magnetic radius is found to be compatible with the current world average. These results demonstrate that BH-dominated EP measurements provide an independent and complementary approach to determine the electromagnetic structure of the proton and offer additional support for the small-radius solution of the proton charge-radius puzzle.

entry.title: Spin-Dependent Nucleon-Nucleus Interactions Constrained by Neutron Observables and Their Impact on Near-Barrier Proton Fusion
entry.summary: We investigate the role of spin-dependent nucleon--nucleus interactions in nuclear reactions. To this end, we use neutron spin observables to constrain the dominant central spin-spin form factors and then apply the corresponding like-channel interactions to near-barrier fusion in the $p+{}^{93}$Nb system. The interactions are constructed within a folding framework based on a finite-range effective nucleon-nucleon force and organized in terms of radial form factors associated with their spin-spin, tensor, and spin-orbit components. Neutron spin observables in the $n$ + $^{27}$Al, $^{59}$Co, and $^{93}$Nb target systems are analyzed within a distorted-wave Born approximation (DWBA) framework {to examine the sign and scale of the central spin-spin contribution and the assembled operator conventions.} The calculation reproduces the observed sign systematics of the neutron spin observables for the three targets, consistent with the dominant central spin-spin contribution in the adopted model. The unlike-channel (neutron--proton) interaction constrained by neutron scattering is then reconstructed for the corresponding like-channel (proton--proton) interaction and applied to a coupled-channels description of near-barrier fusion for the $p+{}^{93}$Nb system. The retained real spin-dependent interactions lead only to a weak modification of the effective barrier and a very small change in the unpolarized fusion cross section within the present model. The present work thus connects the neutron-scattering constraints on the operator conventions with the fusion calculation in the proton channel, and estimates the scale of the corresponding real spin-dependent correction in near-barrier fusion.

entry.title: Homogeneity Pursuit for 3D Point Clouds
entry.summary: This paper proposes a novel classification learning approach to identify the latent group structures in 3D point clouds collected with irregular shapes, which allows 3D point clouds to be classified into different groups with the number of groups and the group membership unknown. 3D point clouds within a group have a common mean function, while mean function heterogeneity is allowed across groups. We first obtain preliminary estimates of the individual mean functions by penalized trivariate splines over triangulation. Based on these preliminary estimates, we develop an agglomerative clustering algorithm to estimate the unknown group structures and propose a ratio criterion to determine the number of groups. We establish the consistency of the estimated number of groups and group membership. Furthermore, we investigate a post-grouping trivariate penalized spline estimation procedure for group-specific mean functions and derive the corresponding asymptotic theory. The proposed method is validated through simulation studies and showcased with an application to the imaging data from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative database.

entry.title: Quantitative approximation theorem of neural operators for the Dirichlet-to-Neumann map
entry.summary: In this paper, we study neural operators for the Dirichet-to-Neumann map (DN map), which is encountered in the famous Calderón's problem. In many numerical methods used for reconstructing the unknown conductivity from the knowledge of the DN map need to evaluate the corresponding DN map at a given conductivity function, which involves solving the boundary value problem for the conductivity equation and taking the Neumann data. Such procedure is time consuming and not effective. Hence, it is a favorable strategy to construct a surrogate to replace the forward map mapping conductivity functions to corresponding DN maps. The main theme of this paper is to derive quantitative bounds on the parametric complexity of these neural operators. In particular, under suitable assumptions, their depth grows at most logarithmically with $\varepsilon^{-1}$, while the relevant spectral and projection ranks grow algebraically. It should be noted that general neural operators suffer from "the curse of parametric dimensionality". This work demonstrates the construction of neural operators for the DN map that does not suffer from such curse.

entry.title: Square-Root Clustered Lasso for High-Dimensional Linear Regression with Finite-Sample Theory and Efficient Algorithm Implementation
entry.summary: This paper proposes a square-root clustered Lasso penalized method for high-dimensional linear regression. By integrating square-root loss with the clustered Lasso penalty, the resulting method enables flexible regression modeling and allows tuning parameter selection independent of the unknown noise level. We establish weak decomposability of the clustered Lasso penalty and a noise-level-free tuning strategy under Gaussian noise. Furthermore, we establish the finite-sample prediction accuracy guarantees for the proposed method. The inherent nonsmoothness of the square-root loss and clustered Lasso penalty poses considerable computational difficulties. To resolve this issue, we develop an efficient semismooth Newton-based proximal augmented Lagrangian algorithm (N-ALM) to solve the corresponding dual optimization problem. The subproblems arising in the iteration are efficiently tackled by the semismooth Newton method, which fully utilizes the sparsity structure of the generalized Jacobian. We further establish global convergence and a local linear rate for the distance to the KKT solution set under suitable conditions; the local rate becomes superlinear when the penalty parameter tends to infinity. We conduct numerical experiments on real-world datasets to evaluate the computational performance of N-ALM. The results demonstrate that N-ALM solves the tested high-dimensional SRCL problems accurately and substantially reduces running times compared with d-ADMM.

entry.title: Being judged through the record: A Rosenhan-inspired test of psychiatric label sensitivity in large language models
entry.summary: The integration of large language models (LLMs) into clinical decision-making raises unresolved questions regarding diagnostic bias. We investigate whether a documented psychiatric history alters LLM recommendations when the current clinical evidence is identical. Using a counterfactual experiment inspired by Rosenhan's 1973 field study, we factorially varied diagnostic-history condition (no prior diagnosis stated vs. prior schizophrenia diagnosis) and current-evidence condition (voices ceased vs. voices persisted) within a clinical vignette. Across five LLMs (GPT-5.6 Sol, Claude Sonnet 5, Gemini 3.6 Flash, Grok 4.6, and Mistral Large 2512), we generated 20,000 model responses across independent queries. When evidence supported discharge, adding a prior schizophrenia diagnosis increased recommendations for continued hospitalization nearly fivefold, from 4.7% to 22.3% (risk difference, 17.5 percentage points; 95% CI, 16.2-18.8). This shift occurred across all five models (risk-difference range, 10.4-34.4 percentage points). In the same condition, reference concordance decreased from 95.3% to 77.7%, while stated decision confidence increased. Across all model-by-evidence contrasts, confidence increases corresponded to Cohen's d values of 0.35-1.09. Signal-detection analyses showed that the prior diagnosis shifted the decision criterion toward hospitalization across all five models and reduced discrimination between the two current-evidence conditions in three of them. When current evidence supported continued hospitalization, the label increased the recommendation for hospitalization from 92.6% to 97.0%.

entry.title: Sparse Target Parameter and Channel Estimation in MIMO-OOFDM-Aided Visible Light Integrated Sensing and Communication Systems
entry.summary: A unified framework is developed for parameter estimation (PE) and channel estimation (CE) in monostatic multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) direct-current-biased optical orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (DCO-OFDM)-aided visible light integrated sensing and communication (VL-ISAC) systems. A common optical waveform supports sensing and downlink communication while accounting for target reflections, clutter, Doppler effects, and the communication channel. For sensing PE, one-dimensional (1D) and two-dimensional (2D) on-grid and off-grid sparse representations are formulated. The proposed 1D off-grid Bayesian learning (1D-OffGBL) algorithm employs a joint delay-Doppler (DD) dictionary to exploit coupled DD information and achieve high estimation accuracy. In contrast, the proposed 2D off-grid Bayesian learning (2D-OffGBL) algorithm sequentially estimates the Doppler and delay parameters, thereby avoiding a high-dimensional joint dictionary and reducing computational complexity. Both algorithms iteratively refine the continuous-valued delay and Doppler parameters to mitigate off-grid basis mismatch. Furthermore, 1D and 2D sparse channel representations and corresponding CE procedures are developed, followed by range and velocity estimation for both sensing models. Closed-form Bayesian Cramer-Rao bounds (BCRBs) are derived for PE, CE, range, and velocity estimation. Simulations demonstrate that the proposed algorithms outperform conventional sparse recovery schemes in terms of normalized mean-squared error (NMSE). In particular, 1D-OffGBL achieves the highest estimation accuracy, whereas 2D-OffGBL provides a favourable performance-complexity trade-off for practical MIMO DCO-OFDM VL-ISAC systems.

entry.title: Probing the Collins effect at photon-photon colliders
entry.summary: We propose to study the Collins effect in the production of almost back-to-back unpolarized hadrons (mainly charged pions) by looking at their azimuthal distributions around the jet thrust-axis in the process $γγ\to h_1h_2X$. The quasi-real photons in the initial state can be emitted either by two scattering leptons or two charged heavy nuclei in ultra-peripheral collisions. We provide numerical estimates for kinematic configurations in principle accessible at the Future Circular Collider and at the planned experiments on ultra-peripheral collisions at the LHC. We find that the corresponding asymmetries can be sizable, even up to around 10-15%. The proposed measurements would thus shed light on the fragmentation mechanism of quarks into hadrons and, in principle, would allow one to distinguish among different existing models for the Collins functions.
